commands.summary: Understand Terraform and OpenTofu as architecture
commands.description:
Rootform turns Terraform and OpenTofu into a semantic, deterministic,
and explainable architecture.

Start with rootform run ./infra to explore a directory locally.
commands.examples:
rootform run ./infra
  rootform build ./infra -o architecture.json
  rootform check ./infra
  rootform diff ./before ./after

flags.usage: show how to use rootform

flags.name: version
flags.usage: print the rootform version and exit

commands.description:
Build a semantic architecture from Terraform or OpenTofu configuration
or from a plan in JSON format.

With no directory, build reads the current directory. --plan reads a plan
instead; use - to read it from standard input. Directory input prepares
missing project dialects before compilation; a coherent local lock is silent.

The Rootform architecture file is written to standard output, or to the
file selected by --output. With --format html the architecture is written
as one page that opens on its own, with no server and no other file.
Diagnostics go to standard error.

Exit status:
  0  the architecture was built
  2  the command was used incorrectly
  3  no complete architecture could be built
commands.examples:
rootform build
  rootform build ./infra
  rootform build ./infra -o architecture.json
  rootform build ./infra --format html -o architecture.html
  rootform build --plan tfplan.json

commands.description:
Build or load an architecture and evaluate the applicable policies.

The input can be an infrastructure directory, a Rootform architecture
file, or - for an architecture file on standard input. With no input,
check reads the current directory. --plan reads a plan in JSON format
instead. Directory input prepares missing project dialects before evaluation;
a coherent local lock is silent.

The selected text, JSON, SARIF, or Markdown result goes to standard
output, or to --output. Diagnostics go to standard error.

Exit status:
  0  every policy passed
  1  at least one policy was violated
  2  the command was used incorrectly
  3  the architecture could not be evaluated
commands.examples:
rootform check
  rootform check ./infra
  rootform check . --locked
  rootform check --plan tfplan.json
  rootform check . --policy-pack ./policies
  rootform build ./infra | rootform check -
  rootform check ./infra --format sarif -o rootform.sarif

commands.description:
Generate a completion script for bash, zsh, fish, or PowerShell.

The script goes to standard output. Diagnostics go to standard error.

Exit status:
  0  the completion script was generated
  1  the completion script could not be generated
  2  the command was used incorrectly
commands.examples:
rootform completion bash > /usr/local/etc/bash_completion.d/rootform
  rootform completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_rootform"
  rootform completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/rootform.fish

flags.name: help
flags.usage: show how to use rootform completion

commands.description:
Compare two architectures and report the architectural changes between
them.

Each input can be an infrastructure directory, a Rootform architecture
file, or - for one architecture file on standard input. --plan reads
both sides from a plan in JSON format instead. Only one input can be -.

The selected text, JSON, or Markdown result goes to standard output, or
to --output. Diagnostics go to standard error.

Exit status:
  0  the comparison succeeded
  1  the architectures differ, and --exit-code was given
  2  the command was used incorrectly
  3  the comparison could not be completed
commands.examples:
rootform diff ./before ./after
  rootform diff before.json after.json --exit-code
  rootform diff --plan tfplan.json
  terraform show -json tfplan | rootform diff --plan -
  rootform diff ./before ./after --format markdown -o rootform-diff.md

declaration was interpreted, or why a policy produced a result.

facts and source locations support it.

By default, explain reads the current directory. --input accepts an
infrastructure directory, a Rootform architecture file, or - for an
architecture file on standard input.

  rootform explain architecture kubernetes_deployment_v1.app --format json
  rootform explain architecture google_compute_network.vpc --input prod.json

commands.description:
Rewrite Rootform source files using the canonical format.

With no path, fmt reads the current directory. By default it rewrites
changed files. --check reports their names and --diff writes changes to

  rootform fmt --check
  rootform fmt ./dialects --diff

commands.description:
Detect providers, resolve Rootform dialects, install missing exact
dialect packages, and write rootform.lock. Path defaults to . and is both the
project and Terraform or OpenTofu root. Unlocked resolution includes the
official index; repeat --source to add a Rootform dialect or index registry
reference. Repeat --policy-pack to select an independent Policy Pack
explicitly.

Machine JSON goes to standard output. Diagnostics and verbose detail go
to standard error.

Exit status:
  0  initialization completed
  1  initialization failed
  2  the command was used incorrectly
  3  no deterministic initialization was available
commands.examples:
rootform init
  rootform init ./infra
  rootform init --source ghcr.io/acme/rootform/company-core:1.2.0
  rootform init --policy-pack ghcr.io/acme/policies:policy-pack-baseline-0.1.0
  rootform init ./infra --no-input
  rootform init ./infra --locked --offline

commands.summary: Publish a verified dialect registry layout
commands.description:
Validate an existing local Rootform registry layout, publish its dialects
to one registry repository, repull every manifest by digest, and verify the
complete dialect set. Use --index to publish the generated index last under
an immutable digest-derived tag. Packaging and dry-run remain offline.

Text or JSON result goes to standard output. Diagnostics go to standard
error.

Exit status:
  0  publication or dry-run verification completed
  2  the command was used incorrectly
  3  publication could not be verified
commands.examples:
rootform publish dialects ./oci --to registry.example/acme/dialects
  rootform publish dialects ./oci --to registry.example/acme/dialects --index
  rootform publish dialects ./oci --to example/dialects --dry-run --format json

commands.description:
Build or load an architecture and check that it is structurally valid
and internally consistent.

The input can be an infrastructure directory, a Rootform architecture
file, or - for an architecture file on standard input. With no input,
validation reads the current directory.

The text or JSON result goes to standard output. Diagnostics go to
standard error.

Exit status:
  0  the architecture is valid
  1  the architecture is not valid
  2  the command was used incorrectly
  3  the architecture could not be validated
commands.examples:
rootform validate architecture
  rootform validate architecture architecture.json
  cat architecture.json | rootform validate architecture -

commands.description:

for reproducible offline use.

commands.description:
Materialize the exact rootform.lock dialect set from the installed
store, content cache, or pinned registry repositories. No version is resolved
and rootform.lock is never changed.

With no --to flag, vendor writes ./.rootform/dialects. Consuming
commands launched from that project root use that directory automatically.
Copied names and versions go to standard output. Diagnostics go to
standard error.

Exit status:
  0  every resolved dialect was copied
  2  the command was used incorrectly
  3  no complete vendored set was written
commands.examples:
rootform init . --no-input
  rootform vendor dialects
  rootform vendor dialects --to ./offline/dialects

flags.usage: show how to use rootform vendor dialects

commands.description:
Materialize the exact rootform.lock Policy Pack set from the installed
store, content cache, or each pinned registry repository. No version is
resolved and rootform.lock is never changed.

With no --to flag, vendor writes ./.rootform/policy-packs. Policy-aware
commands use that directory exclusively when present.

Copied names and versions go to standard output. Diagnostics go to
standard error.

Exit status:

  2  the command was used incorrectly
  3  no complete vendored set was written
commands.examples:

  rootform vendor policy-packs
